To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the attributes most important to the work environment of veterinary clinical teachers are knowledge and enthusiasm, whereas scholarly activity is least valued; and that, although all groups agree that teaching is a primary role, faculty and students feel that clinical service is equally important, while CTS consider teaching as their primary role.
the most important attributes of effective veterinary clinical teachers are competence-knowledge and enthusiasm; the three least important are scholarly activity and lack of bias.

veterinary clinical teachers are expected to be competent, to have enthusiasm, and to be able to respect the independence of the learners they teach, and to invest most effort in the activity of teaching.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the personal attributes of effective clinical veterinary teachers and the activities in which clinical veterinary teachers should invest most of their effort.
the identification of personal attributes in veterinary clinicians that are valued most and least by their work environment.
how veterinary clinical teachers are viewed by the various groups with whom they work and how these views differ between the groups.
